a: A cool roof is a roof made highly reflective and highly emissive. Most often, a light-coloured coating is applied to the existing roof covering: it sends back most of the solar radiation and quickly releases the remaining heat.
As a result, the roof heats up far less and transmits less heat to the building.

The studies reviewed by the US Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) report a roof 28 to 33 °C cooler at the height of summer, air-conditioning savings of 2 to over 40% (20% on average) and peak demand reductions of 14 to 38%.
These figures vary widely from one building to another: roof insulation, use, air conditioning, climate. Our preliminary study is used to estimate the value for your building.

q: Does a cool roof increase heating in winter?
a: Slightly, because the roof also captures less sunlight in winter. But the sun is then low and the days are short: in most of the climates studied, this penalty remains smaller than the summer savings (US EPA).

It weighs more for a building that is mainly heated, in a cold climate. A study carried out for the French Building Federation found a very small effect when heating accounts for 75% of the needs, and a favourable balance as soon as air conditioning exceeds 30% of the needs. We take this into account in our study.

q: Which roofs can it be applied to?
a: Most flat and low-pitched roofs: metal deck, bituminous or synthetic waterproofing, concrete. Fibre cement sheets require an asbestos survey first.
A roof covering that is too damaged must first be repaired or replaced. For reflective paints, roofs where water ponds must be excluded.

q: Do operations have to stop during the works?
a: Generally not: the works take place on the roof, from the outside. We organise access, working hours and safety zones with you so as not to disrupt operations.

It depends on the country. In France, under conditions, CEE sheet BAT-EN-112 funds the application of a reflective coating on the roof of tertiary buildings in commercial use, above an air-conditioned volume, with a coating whose SRI exceeds 100 when new and 90 after ageing.
Spain created an energy-saving certificate system in 2023, and in Switzerland the rules and any support depend on the canton. We check what applies to your project during the study.
